questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Simultaneous Solubility with Common Ion Effect
questions.question: A buffer solution in [Equilibrium (Chemical & Ionic)] contains $0.1\text{ M}$ acetic acid $(\text{p}K_a = 4.74)$ and $0.1\text{ M}$ sodium acetate. If $0.02\text{ moles}$ of solid $\text{NaOH}$ are added to $1\text{ L}$ of this buffer, what is the new $\text{pH}$? $(\log 1.5 = 0.18)$
questions.solution: Added $\text{OH}^-$ neutralizes acid: $[\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}] = 0.1 - 0.02 = 0.08\text{ M}$, $[\text{CH}_3\text{COO}^-] = 0.1 + 0.02 = 0.12\text{ M}$. By Henderson equation: $\text{pH} = \text{p}K_a + \log\frac{[\text{salt}]}{[\text{acid}]} = 4.74 + \log\frac{0.12}{0.08} = 4.74 + \log(1.5) = 4.74 + 0.18 = 4.92$.
questions.explanation: Analyze using fundamental chemical principles in Equilibrium (Chemical & Ionic).
tags: Simultaneous Solubility with Common Ion Effect

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Simultaneous Solubility with Common Ion Effect
questions.question: What is the basicity (number of ionizable hydrogen atoms per molecule) of pyrophosphoric acid $(\text{H}_4\text{P}_2\text{O}_7)$ in [Equilibrium (Chemical & Ionic)]?
questions.solution: Pyrophosphoric acid contains two tetrahedral phosphorus atoms connected by a $\text{P-O-P}$ bridge, with four $-\text{OH}$ groups attached directly to phosphorus. All four hydrogens are acidic, so its basicity is $4$.
questions.explanation: Calculate using quantitative laws in Equilibrium (Chemical & Ionic).
tags: Simultaneous Solubility with Common Ion Effect

questions.question: What is the basicity (number of ionizable hydrogen atoms per molecule) of pyrophosphoric acid $(\text{H}_4\text{P}_2\text{O}_7)$ in [Equilibrium (Chemical & Ionic)]?
questions.solution: Pyrophosphoric acid contains two tetrahedral phosphorus atoms connected by a $\text{P-O-P}$ bridge, with four $-\text{OH}$ groups attached directly to phosphorus. All four hydrogens are acidic, so its basicity is $4$.
questions.explanation: Calculate using quantitative laws in Equilibrium (Chemical & Ionic).
